counterfactual_missing_items: No objective evidence of retinal edema or commotio retinae on fundoscopy
No afferent pupillary defect or VEP abnormality to support optic neuropathy
No focal neurologic deficit or imaging abnormality to support traumatic brain injury
decisive_items: the patient was referred for psychiatric evaluation to rule out conversion disorder
Anterior and posterior segment examinations, relative afferent pupillary defect testing, fogging test, and menace reflex were all normal
Visual evoked potentials were normal, and electroretinography indicated no pathologic process
response.rationale: R4 aligns with the complete clinical picture: acute bilateral painless vision loss with entirely normal ocular, neurologic, and electrophysiologic examinations, prompting psychiatric referral. R3 is contradicted by normal VEPs and lacks bilateral optic nerve findings. R1 and R2 are unsupported by normal fundoscopy and imaging.

rejected.why: Commotio retinae requires retinal whitening/edema on fundoscopy, which is explicitly normal; no supportive raw span.
Concussion alone does not explain bilateral no-light-perception vision loss with normal brain imaging and neurologic exam.
Traumatic optic neuropathy is typically unilateral and would show abnormal VEPs or RAPD; both are normal here.
